title: Day 32 — Cross-Language Contract
prompt: Our Python server rejects the TS client's request body — the schemas have drifted. There's a documented contract. Make the client match it. Where do you start?

clarifications.answer: The server expects snake_case keys (user_id, full_name, email_verified, created_at). No camelCase.
created_at is an ISO string via new Date(ms).toISOString(), not the raw epoch-ms number the client holds.
tags must be sorted ascending — and don't mutate the caller's array; sort a copy.
referrer is nullable but always present: user.referrer ?? null. Never drop the key.
CONTRACT.md is the source of truth — match it exactly; the tests encode it.
Sort a COPY of tags ([...tags].sort()) so you don't mutate the caller's data.

hints: Open CONTRACT.md and the current output side by side; list every difference before editing.
Five things: snake_case keys, ISO timestamp, sorted tags (copy!), null-but-present referrer.
Return one object literal with snake_case keys; new Date(user.createdAtMs).toISOString(); [...user.tags].sort(); user.referrer ?? null.
